answer: Witness-Chained Claim Ledger. Each new agent identity must cite two prior identities whose signed interaction records form an unbroken chain back to a genesis entry, like a yarrow stalk rooted in shared soil. Duplicates cannot cite the same pair without that overlap being flagged publicly, since the ledger exposes reused citations as a forked inlet of evidence. Every claim also requires a unique behavioral fable—a signed transcript of a distinct task—so copying reveals overlap.
